match_note: Communications Materials file (manuscript previously reviewed at another journal; only Comms Mater rounds included). Version 0 comments match arXiv v1: v1 quotes the c-axis length from XRD in Methods but shows no XRD data, uses the 'whether the localized state is a boson or a fermion' and 'Bose glass phase between the superconducting and Mott insulating phases' wording R2 objects to, sets p=1 in Eq. (1), has samples 1-7 with Fig. 2(b) ln T fits, and its p.8 last paragraph is the nickelate/perovskite outlook the rebuttal says was rewritten. XRD figure S1, the expanded Methods and the crossover wording were added after v1.

concerns.quote: The connection with high-Tc perovskite superconductors that is stated already in the abstract is not clear.
concerns.summary: The motivating link to high-Tc perovskite (cuprate) superconductors in the abstract is unexplained.

concerns.quote: The article is not written in a comprehensive way with a specific train of thought and there are jumps between arguments.
Most parts are referred to other articles, hence can not be easily evaluated. The article should be self-containedas mucgh as possible.
concerns.summary: The paper relies too heavily on cited work and is not self-contained.

concerns.quote: There is even no detailed information on how the samples are prepared.
concerns.summary: Sample preparation is not described (only referred to another article), so samples cannot be evaluated or reproduced.

concerns.quote: The Authors discuss XRD and lattice distortions, but there are no XRD data shown in this article.
concerns.summary: Lattice distortion is invoked but no structural (XRD) data on the studied samples are shown.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The authors also did not give a reason why and how the distortion affects the electron correlations.
concerns.summary: No mechanism is given for how RuO6 distortion changes correlations, so it is unclear whether the transitions are correlation- or disorder-driven.

concerns.quote: The magnetization measurement and diamagnetism transition observation is required to confirm and support this idea.
concerns.summary: The proposed link between diamagnetism and Cooper-pair localization needs magnetization measurements on these samples.

concerns.quote: Most importantly, the samples seem to show random behaviours.
concerns.summary: Samples of nearly equal thickness (25 and 30 nm) behave oppositely, contradicting the claim that thinning drives the phase transitions.

concerns.quote: The sample with 10nm of thickness shows lower Tc than that of 30 nm.
concerns.summary: The thinner 10 nm sample has lower Tc than the 30 nm one, and the cause of this non-monotonic behaviour is not discussed.

concerns.quote: The Authors claim that the MBE samples suffer distortion, however, they are closer to the critical point than sample 2
concerns.summary: MBE films, claimed to be more distorted, sit closer to the critical point than a thicker undistorted sample, which is unexplained.

concerns.quote: Page 8, the last paragraph is not clear and should be revised.
concerns.summary: The last paragraph on page 8 is unclear.

concerns.quote: The conclusions are not delivering to the reader the impact of the results reported and the future developments of this work.
concerns.summary: The conclusions are too technical and do not convey impact or outlook.

concerns.quote: The transition between Bose glass and Fermi glass based on scaling of resistivity has been studied in Ref. [11] by some of the authors
concerns.summary: The Bose glass-Fermi glass scaling analysis was already published by overlapping authors, limiting novelty.

concerns.quote: The temperature range where the conductivity shows lnT behavior in Fig.2(b) is too narrow. One at least need |\Delta lnT|>1
concerns.summary: The ln T fitting range is too narrow to establish logarithmic behaviour.

concerns.quote: the resistivity/conductivity does not show any anomaly at the temperature the authors marked as a transition. It is at most a crossover
concerns.summary: The marked Fermi glass-Mott and Fermi glass-Bose glass 'transitions' show no anomaly and are at most crossovers.

concerns.quote: Is there any physical insight to set p=1 in Eq. (1)?
concerns.summary: The choice p=1 for the dephasing exponent is unjustified and its relation to inelastic scattering unclear.
Statements such as a localized state being a boson or fermion, and a Bose glass between SC and Mott phases in a QPT, are physically incorrect.

later_concerns.quote: this finding does not constitute direct evidence of RuO6 distortion.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: a c-axis parameter difference (possibly strain) does not establish RuO6 distortion or its effect on correlations and localization; main conclusion unsupported.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the exact relationship linking lattice distortion, electron correlations, and carrier localization has yet to be convincingly resolved.
later_concerns.summary: Round 3: even with all lattice constants, the link between distortion, correlations and localization remains unresolved.
